nodes.desc: A key building block in the petrochemical industry, used to make polyethylene, ethylene oxide, and more.
A major monomer used in the production of polypropylene and various propylene oxide derivatives.
An aromatic hydrocarbon used mainly to produce polystyrene and various copolymers like ABS and SAN.
An important diene widely used as a monomer in the production of synthetic rubbers and polymer resins.
A reactive monomer used in the production of polyacrylonitrile, ABS plastics, and specialized synthetic rubbers.
The primary precursor to polyvinyl chloride (PVC), a versatile and widely used plastic.
A key starting material for the synthesis of polycarbonates and epoxy resins.
An organic compound used primarily as a monomer in the production of nylon 6 (PA6).
A major precursor used in the manufacture of polyester resins like PET and PBT.
Used alongside terephthalic acid to produce PET, also a common antifreeze agent.
A highly reactive molecule used as an industrial building block for polycarbonates and polyurethanes.
Polyethylene: the most widely produced plastic in the world, utilized in packaging, pipes, and more.
High-density Polyethylene: known for its high strength-to-density ratio, used in hard containers and pipes.
Low-density Polyethylene: flexible and tough, typically used for plastic bags and general films.
Linear Low-density Polyethylene: offers greater toughness and puncture resistance than LDPE.
Ethylene-vinyl acetate: an elastomeric polymer that produces materials which are 'rubber-like' in softness and flexibility.
Polypropylene: rugged and unusually resistant to many chemical solvents, bases and acids.
Polystyrene: a strong plastic created from styrene, often used in protective packaging and food containers.
Expanded Polystyrene: a lightweight rigid cellular plastic used primarily in insulation and packaging.
Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene: an opaque thermoplastic polymer offering incredible impact resistance and toughness.
Styrene Acrylonitrile: a copolymer plastic combining the clarity of polystyrene with the toughness of acrylonitrile.
Polyvinyl Chloride: the world's third-most widely produced synthetic plastic polymer, used heavily in construction.
Polycarbonate: a strong, tough material, highly impact resistant, and some grades are optically transparent.
Polyamide 6 (Nylon 6): offers excellent mechanical toughness and chemical resistance, used in fibers and engineering plastics.
Polyethylene Terephthalate: commonly used for fibers for clothing, food packaging, and liquid containers.
Polybutylene Terephthalate: a thermoplastic engineering polymer used heavily as an electrical insulator.
